facts.raw_span: A 52-year-old woman
history of long-standing diplopia
persistent vertical misalignment
anomalous band in the right orbit
surgically excised without improvement in motility
diplopia remained stable in primary gaze
orthotropic in primary position
elevation deficit of the right eye
The globes were unremarkable with no measured proptosis
retroocular fat, optic nerves and sheaths, optic chiasm, and brain parenchyma appeared normal
right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion
it was unchanged from the previous study

concepts.why: The presence of an anomalous band in the right orbit and a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion medial to the medial rectus muscle, with characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle, suggests a possible diagnosis of orbital fibrosis.
The history of long-standing diplopia and elevation deficit of the right eye, combined with the presence of a soft-tissue lesion in the orbit, could be indicative of thyroid eye disease.
The presence of an anomalous band in the right orbit and a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion, with no other clear cause, could suggest a diagnosis of idiopathic orbital inflammation.
The elevation deficit of the right eye and the presence of a soft-tissue lesion in the orbit, with characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle, could be indicative of orbital myositis.

rationales.F04: The presence of an anomalous band in the right orbit suggests a possible orbital fibrosis or inflammation.
rationales.F11: The right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion is consistent with orbital fibrosis or inflammation.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion with signal-intensity characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle, unchanged from the previous study, supports Orbital fibrosis as the most likely diagnosis.
